Byrne was officially named the sixth head coach of the Charlotte 49ers women's soccer program on October 17, 2025, in the midst of overseeing one of the most successful campaigns over the last decade for the Niners in her first season with the Green and White.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHired as an assistant coach in January 2025, Byrne was elevated to interim head coach shortly after her arrival in April of the same year. After Charlotte was picked 10th in the American Conference Preseason Coaches' poll heading into the 2025 campaign, Byrne led the Niners to the No. 2 seed in the Conference Tournament, the highest postseason tournament ranking for the program since 2013. She became the fifth coach to guide the program to double-digit wins in her debut season, with the Niners finishing 10-6-2 under her tutelage for the most wins and conference wins in a season since 2019. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nByrne helped engineer an immediate turnaround for a Niners side that finished with a record of 4-8-7 in 2024, with the team racking up 29 goals and 21 assists after tallies of 13 and 12 respectively in the previous campaign. Under the first-year coach, six Charlotte players were named All-Conference selections, the most since 2016, including a First Team nod for senior Megan Bradley. Additionally, Niners were selected seven times for individual American Conference Weekly Awards (the most since 2009) and collected a total of 16 total appearances on the Conference's Weekly Awards list, the most ever for the program. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nCharlotte also ranked as high as 36th in the NCAA RPI Rankings in Byrne's first season at the helm \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nA native of Coventry, England, arrived in Charlotte after six years at the Savannah College of Art and Design, spending five years at SCAD as an assistant coach before serving as the associate head coach this past fall. She helped the Bees win back-to-back Sun Conference regular season and tournament championships in 2023 and 2024 and won the 2024 NAIA Women's Soccer Championship. Byrne coached two First Team All-Americans and the United Soccer Coaches NAIA Player of the Year last fall en route to being part of the NAIA's Coaching Staff of the Year after winning the national title.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nShe helped lay the groundwork for SCAD's championship in 2021 by breaking multiple program records and winning a postseason match for the first time while reaching a year-end ranking of No. 18 in the NAIA Coaches Poll. The 2021 Bees broke program records for points (189), shots (455), assists (57), and matches played (21) while scoring the second-most goals (66) and winning the second-most matches (13) in a single year in program history. She also has experience in the WPSL, including being named the WPSL Coach of the Year during the 2021-22 campaign.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nByrne grew up playing for Coventry City Ladies and was eventually named captain of her club and college teams. She had a two-year stint as an assistant coach at Southwestern College before joining SCAD and holds a USSF B license, United Soccer Coaches level one and two goalkeeping licenses, UEFA Football Association level one and two certificates. Byrne is also a member of the US Soccer SheChampions cohort.\u003Cbr Yohn was hired as an assistant coach for Charlotte Women's Soccer in February of 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn her first season with the Niners, Yohn oversaw a career-best campaign from transfer goalkeeper Harlee Head, who notched four shutouts on the way to a Third Team All-American Conference nod under Yohn's mentorship as the Green and White allowed a goal or fewer in 12 games. Head would finish fourth in the American Conference in both goals against average (1.20) and shutouts while placing sixth in both saves (69) and saves per game (3.83), all of which were career-high marks in her first season in Charlotte; she was also twice named the American Conference Goalkeeper of the Week and an Honorable Mention once. \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nYohn comes to Charlotte after two years as the Goalkeeper Coach at Howard University, where she helped the Bison reach the conference semifinals in the Northeast Conference both seasons. Howard swept both the regular season and conference tournament championships this past year in 2024, putting the Bison back in the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2018. Yohn's work with goalkeeper Trinity Knox played a big role in Howard's success the last two seasons as Knox took home back-to-back NEC Goalkeeper of the Year awards, in addition to the Bison sweeping the NEC Defensive, Midfield, Rookie, and Coach of the Year awards.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBefore her time at Howard, Yohn served as a volunteer assistant at West Virginia, serving as WVU's goalkeeper coach and assisting with the team's daily training sessions. In 2022 she helped the Mountaineers win the Big 12 Tournament Championship and advance to the second round of the NCAA Tournament. Yohn helped Kayza Massey win Big 12 Co-Goalkeeper of the Year honors in addition to United Soccer Coaches All-Midwest Region Third Team and All-Big 12 First Team selections. Massey backstopped West Virginia to 10 shutouts that year - the 13th-most clean sheets in the nation, and a .786 save percentage while becoming the first goalkeeper in program history to be named a conference Goalkeeper of the Year.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nYohn began her coaching career back at Howard as a volunteer assistant, helping the Bison win the Southwestern Athletic Conference Regular-Season title and finish as a finalist in the SWAC Tournament in 2019. Howard's keeper took home First Team All-SWAC honors that year and was named the league's Goalkeeper of the Year.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nYohn played her collegiate soccer in the Big Ten at Purdue from 2014-17. She served as a team captain her senior year and helped guide the Boilermakers to the program's first postseason appearance in nine seasons. Yohn still ranks inside Purdue's top-10 career ranks for goalkeepers in minutes played, wins, save percentage, and fewest goals allowed. Yohn also took home three consecutive Academic All-Big Ten honors and was a two-time Big Ten Distinguished Scholar.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nYohn holds a USSF \"B\" License and a USSF Goalkeeping
